title: Bounded original equations generate the polynomial fibre kernel locally
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $S$ an $R$-algebra, $q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$, $n\in\mathbb N$, and $\varphi:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow S$ a surjective $R$-algebra map [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Write $p=q\cap R$, $Q=\varphi^{-1}(q)$, $I=\ker\varphi$, and $A=P_Q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Assume the prime of $\kappa(p)\otimes_R S$ corresponding to $q$ has a principal neighbourhood which is a global complete intersection over $\kappa(p)$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Then there exist $c\le n$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in P$ such that $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)\subseteq I$ and $IA\subseteq JA+pA$. No flatness or finite-generation hypothesis on $I$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 00SY, proof of (3) implies (2), equations and flatness paragraphs; Tag 00SC. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00SY and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00SC.

proof.text: Apply the natural polynomial fibre comparison to obtain a prime t of the quotient by Ibar, a CI neighbourhood at t, and e:A/pA to k[x] localized at the inverse-image prime of t, taking the image of IA to Ibar localized there.

Apply the existing conormal rank theorem at t: obtain d and a basis of the localized conormal module of Ibar indexed by Fin(n-d). The polynomial ring over k is Noetherian, so Ibar is finite. Apply the finite-ideal conormal generator bound to this basis to get spanFinrank of the localized ideal at most n-d, hence at most n.

Let K be the image of IA in A/pA. Mapping across e identifies K with the localized ideal Ibar. The ring-equivalence ideal-map identity transfers finite generation, and spanFinrank is unchanged by a ring equivalence, so K is finite with spanFinrank at most n. Choose a finite minimal generating set s for K. For each x in s, quotient surjectivity lifts x to y in IA. Localization ideal membership supplies f in I and a denominator t outside Q with y(t/1)=f/1. Therefore x times the unit image of t/1 equals the image of f/1. Enumerate s by Fin(c), c=spanFinrank K, obtaining f_i in I. Unit cancellation makes their images span K. Taking the inverse image under A to A/pA gives IA contained in (f_i)A+pA. This is the fully proved private lifting lemma in the item module; it does not assume I finite.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00SY (3) implies (2), selection of equations; Tag 00SC conormal rank and Tag 00DV Nakayama. K2: polynomial fibre comparison and generic Nakayama bound are fully proved, and original equation lifting is explicit.
